全成就了，回来补个好评。

如果对上了电波将会是相当优秀且耐玩的游戏，换言之就是优缺点都非常明显。

剧情一般（需要 Is the order a DLC 补全体验），音乐顶级，画面以十年前的标准来说还行，弹幕设计相当华丽且有记忆点（躲起来手感如何你先别问），在游戏本体完成度极高的同时兼顾了 0% 物品挑战、special boss 挑战、boss rush 挑战等内容，使得其游戏寿命非常长，还有很多可以开发的奇妙小技巧（比如紫 boost 暴击）。

问题的话，我觉得最大的问题还是道中：除了地图背景的美术风格以外，道中感觉全长一个样……放怪基本上是四色战队轮着来，在雪地就放蓝色的怪，在火山就放黄色和红色的怪，这啥啊……高难度下跑图受伤惩罚还贼重，还让不让人愉快地玩平台跳跃了……

喜欢我长按攻击键显示判断点吗，喜欢我双脚沾地躲超高速奇偶奇偶奇吗，喜欢我近战卡肉被自己硬控2秒但是其余东西速度不变吗
如在自动存档的地方卡关了的话,可以从主选单读取之前的手动存档喔!
如果是冲类银河恶魔城来的要注意，这游戏的卖点是可爱的女角色和百合，关卡虽然确实是类银河恶魔城的设计，但BOSS战却是弹幕游戏

Rabi-Ribi is a great metroidvania with varied locales, rewarding exploration, enough cues to guide a player combined a plethora of options to enable sequence breaking and good bosses. Items are regularly powerful, there's several major progression enabling items that let you into new areas and a bunch of other solid general power ups - both always feel good to find. The game controls well at all times and mistakes are almost always your own (with the exception of one attack which I preferred to turn off). The world is easy to navigate with numerous warps and terrain and areas feel distinct enough to path using without needing to pull up a map to make sure you're 'somewhere new yet' or similar.

That said, the game isn't without some minor gripes. Every single character design - and by extension almost all of the bosses - are some variety of anime girl (they will greet you and then decide they need to shoot bullet hell patterns at you). The lack of diversity is a complete non-issue for me, the bullet patterns are always highly varied and you will need to be applying yourself to learn new attacks and positioning which stops things from ever dragging but I can completely understand that some people would prefer a more traditional variety of platformer bosses which are simply not present here. The general minions have a good variety of attacks but are again mostly cute animals or anime girls themed around animals; if you are put off by the very anime aesthetics this is a lot more likely to grate on you than it ever did on me. The plot insomuch as it exists is similarly one dimensional and is basically cute girls doing silly things and magic. Sometimes that's all you need, cute things are cute, you know?

Outside of the above, the map could also do with a pin system (and honestly just an automated uncollected icon for everything you see exposed but can't collect), the warp menu could be better organised and present more information and the platforming in general could do with having more teeth to it before the postgame areas but none of these take away from the overabundance of quality in the exploration and bosses which are the clear focus. In spite of the ease of navigation the terrain in general could also be of a bit higher fidelity but it's a very minor nitpick. 

If you aren't filtered by the art style and the fact the story is very surface level slice of life anime with very minimal justification of a focus on kemonomimi designs there's an incredibly rewarding exploration platformer with some stellar progression and some great bullet hell bosses in a game that's a joy to play from start to finish. 

Strongly recommended, I look forward to the sequel which I will join my brothers in playing naked day 1.

Rabi-Ribi is sold as both metroidvania and bullet hell. The story is about a rabbit turned human and her quest to find her owners lost sister. To do so you run around in the wilderness and find people to fight and invite back to the town so you can use a magical mcguffin to make repeated journeys to a strange dimension in an effort to save the sister.

On the metroidvania side of things Rabi-Ribi has lots of little things to find that give you a nice little dopamine boost but in the end do very little to enhance the actual gameplay. A small percentile increase to your pitiful damage. Or how about a 1.5% increase to your stamina that is completely empty after one combo anyways? While actually exciting upgrades like slide or double jump are hard locked behind story progress. Trying to enter those areas leads to your character and company literally saying 'I don't feel like going there'. At least until you progressed far enough into the story and one of the people you beat up tells you about someone else to beat up in that formerly inaccessible part.

Combat against regular enemies was kind of boring most of the time and frustrating the rest. Most enemies were no real threat as they deal little damage and die in just a couple of hits. Some others like to spam randomly moving shapes all over the screen which just made map traversal annoying. Enemy variety is also rather low. Most of the enemies are (fake) bunny girls, and a lot of palette swapped fish, fairies, mushrooms and the like.

On the bullet hell side of things there is the boss combat. Initially fun with different bosses of course having slightly different movesets and their own personality in some of their attack patterns and choice of offensive weaponry. But these will start feel samey the longer the game goes on. Boss health and their damage dealt scales with either story progress + collected items or just story progress depending on your choice. And while the game tells us that items will always benefit the player more than the bosses, that doesn't stop it from giving bosses health in the thousands while you're well away from breaking triple digit damage. Due to cheap recovery items and a certain magic attack I was rarely in danger of dying but at a point these fights just start to overstay their welcome because of how long they take. 
Also this might just be an issue for me but I don't like that there is no indicator of Erinas hitbox. Especially since later fights turn into a mess of overlapping effects and stuff just happening on your screen

I give Rabi-Ribi a thumbs down. Maybe I expected the wrong things from these tags. But for me it just falls flat in the exploration with items being locked because the characters refusing to go where I want. And while the boss fights were a welcome break from the exploration part of the game, they just got more and more tedious as time went on.

可以说是被可爱画风掩盖的硬核杰作。在独立游戏如繁星般涌现的今天，有一款2016年悄然登陆Steam的作品，以其看似“肤浅”的可爱外表，包裹着一个令核心玩家惊叹的深度内核——《拉比哩比》。

一、 反差的魅力：从“艹兔”到弹幕地狱
《拉比哩比》常被玩家戏称为“艹兔”，这一昵称源自其可爱的日系动漫美术风格。游戏讲述了原本是普通兔子的艾莉娜，在某天醒来后发现自己身处未知之地并变成了人类兔女郎，随后在活泼的小妖精莉波陪伴下，踏上寻找家园之旅。仅看立绘、CG和角色设定，很容易将其误判为一款轻松休闲的“萌系”游戏。

然而，这正是制作团队精心设计的最大“陷阱”。一旦进入实际游玩，玩家将迎面撞上的是设计极其精密、难度极高的弹幕地狱式BOSS战。游戏提供了多达6种难度选项，从“简单”模式下几乎不会受伤的体验，到最高难度下如同东方Project般密集华丽的弹幕演出，确保了从新手到骨灰级玩家都能找到适合自己的挑战。这种极致的反差——用最可爱的角色演绎最硬核的战斗——构成了《拉比哩比》独一无二的魅力核心。正如一位Reddit玩家所言，这款游戏在机制深度上与《黑暗之魂》、《鬼泣》和《恶魔城》的共通点，远多于其外表所暗示的任何作品。

二、 顶级的类银河战士恶魔城设计：自由与深度的完美融合
《拉比哩比》在Metroidvania的游戏结构设计上达到了近乎教科书级别的水准，其核心优势体现在惊人的非线性与可拓展性上。极致的非线性与序列破坏（Sequence Breaking）：游戏拥有一个广阔的互联世界，包含9个主要区域和超过20个子区域。与许多同类游戏不同，《拉比哩比》几乎不强制玩家的探索顺序。游戏虽有剧情提示，但玩家完全可以按照自己的喜好规划路线。更令人惊叹的是其顶级的序列破坏设计。高级玩家甚至可以达成“0%收集通关”，即在不获取任何关键道具（包括主武器） 的情况下完成游戏。这种设计赋予了游戏极高的重复可玩性，每次通关都可以尝试不同的道具获取顺序和探索路线，其自由度在同类游戏中少有匹敌，有评论认为或许只有《空洞骑士》能与之相近。玩家控制近战攻击的艾莉娜，并间接操控负责远程攻击的莉波。通过探索广大的地图并收集散布各处的超过60种道具和能力，角色的能力将逐步提升，解锁新的区域。场景中充满了需要特定技能（如二段跳、滑行）才能获取的隐藏物品，极大地激励玩家进行重复探索与解谜。这种“获得能力-解锁新区域-发现秘密”的正向循环被设计得流畅而富有满足感。

三、 战斗系统的深度：从近战连段到弹幕华尔兹
本作的战斗系统是近战格斗与弹幕射击的精妙结合。艾莉娜使用玩具槌进行近战攻击，并能在流程中学到进阶连段技巧；莉波则负责蓄力光束等远程攻击。玩家需要同时兼顾两者的位置与输出节奏，操作上限极高。这是游戏最耀眼的部分。游戏拥有超过40场独特的BOSS战斗，攻击模式更是多达上千种。每一场BOSS战都是一场精心编排的弹幕演出，玩家需要在狭小的空间内闪转腾挪，于弹幕的缝隙中寻找攻击时机。更可贵的是，游戏不同难度不仅改变数值，更是彻底改变了BOSS的行为模式和弹幕设计，在高难度下会面对更快、更复杂的新攻击，使得多周目挑战始终充满新鲜感，这一设计被玩家盛赞远超许多仅提供NG+模式的类魂游戏。除了主线20-40小时的流程，游戏还提供了Boss Rush模式、Speedrun模式（去除剧情纯竞速），以及可操作角色可可亚（Cocoa）的特殊模式，她拥有与艾莉娜完全不同的玩法和序列破坏方式。后续更新与DLC（白金版）更是增加了如数字艺术书、交响乐模式等额外内容，将游戏体量扩充到一个惊人的程度。

四、 其他亮点与综合评价
游戏拥有超过50首原创曲目，这些音乐不仅数量庞大，而且质量上乘、非常耐听，完美烘托了不同场景的氛围，从轻松悠扬的城镇音乐到紧张激烈的BOSS战配乐，都令人印象深刻。游戏支持包括简繁中文、英文、日文、法文、德文、西班牙文在内的多种语言，显示了开发者面向全球市场的诚意。评论普遍称赞其扎实的游戏内容、刺激的战斗体验和极高的自由度，但也指出其剧情和人物刻画相对薄弱。最大的争议点无疑在于其画风，这既是其独特的标签，也成了阻碍更多玩家尝试的门槛。

总结
在类银河战士恶魔城这个类型中，它在非线性设计、BOSS战深度、难度调节灵活性和内容量方面都树立了极高的标杆。如果你是一位热爱挑战、钟情于探索与战斗深度、不以外表判游戏的玩家，那么错过《拉比哩比》将是一个巨大的遗憾。它不仅仅是一款优秀的独立游戏，更是证明了“游戏性”永远凌驾于“画风”之上的绝佳例证。这款由港台团队精心打造的杰作，值得每一个核心玩家献上敬意。

Fui jogar isso no meme, fui surpreendido com um algo super divertido e desafiador, e um metroidvania muito peculiar. Entrou facilmente em um dos meus favoritos, e fiz questão de platiná-lo antes de escrever isso.
Antes de qualquer coisa, já deixo claro que esse jogo super vale a compra, e se decidir jogá-lo, compre o pacote "Super UPRPRC Edition", as DLCs trazem o endgame final que termina a campanha do jogo, e conteúdos que fazem do jogo realmente completo. Sem elas, não é possível platinar o jogo. Mas! O pacote é super barato em uma promoção, ficando apenas 40 reais!

O jogo pode ser bem resumido como metroidvania e bullet hell. Mas, além dos chefes, o que torna tão divertido são também os controles e movimentação geral ao navegar pelo mapa. Tudo funciona super bem, e você realmente sente sua progressão ao decorrer do jogo. O mapa é grandinho, e é recheado de segredos, que recompensa bastante com pequenos upgrades que se acumulam rapidamente, e habilidades que acrescentam muito.

E ainda mais do que isso, muita coisa te impressiona quando você descobre a quantidade de alternativas você pode tomar durante o jogo. Existem "técnicas secretas" que são capacidades de movimentação que é possível utilizar desde o início do jogo (alá Super Metroid com o Wall Jump), que permite sua progressão tomar rumos bizarros.
E tudo isso é complementado pelas conquistas desse jogo, são elas que te motivam, te instigam curiosidade, e até te ensinam tais técnicas (ou te dizem COMO você fez, caso realize alguma sem querer), e esfrega na sua cara o quanto o jogo tem sua progressão não linear. E para complementar, em tais progressões, o jogo literalmente se adapta para que certas sessões e até ataques de chefes sejam possíveis em uma run Low%, por exemplo.

Junto disso, as conquistas exploram super bem quase cada cantinho e desafio que o jogo tem a oferecer, algumas são bem brutais, mas são legais. Caçar elas traz uma baita variedade e valor de replay que faz você ir aprendendo cada vez mais do jogo. Vale super a pena, com certeza uma das minhas platinas favoritas!

No mais, a variedade de inimigos é só ok, eles são só algo que passamos sem pensar muito, mas existem bons desafios de plataforma, e os chefes são bem bacanas, alguns bem irritantes também kkkkkk. E o combate consegue ter muita profundidade em combos e na variedade de estratégias/playstyles que são viáveis.

Rabi-Ribi é bom demais.
